title: Aurum Alpha personal-data inventory
description: standards/082-data-subject-rights.md DR1: the declaration, committed in the repository beside the schema, of every store that holds data about a person. One entry per (store, subject column); a store with two columns naming people carries two entries, each with its own treatment, because erasure targets a subject and not a row. The export job and the erasure job are functions of this file and of nothing else, which is why a store holding personal data with no entry is a finding rather than an oversight. The conditional rules below are DR5's treatment vocabulary made mechanical: a retained entry names its legal basis and what survives; an anonymised entry names what survives, as an allowlist; a deleted entry names neither; an entry declared free of personal data says why and can be exported by nothing. schema_version 1 - evolves additively per PC6.

identifier.description: A table, collection, bucket-prefix, provider or column name, snake_case per 025 SD10. Never a hostname or a connection string: the entry names the store logically and configuration says where it is.

duration.description: ISO 8601 duration. Retention windows are years and months, so the calendar components are admitted here where 057's job durations admit only days and time.

legalBasis.description: DR5. Why a row survives an erasure request, stated so a checker can require the answer and a lawyer can read it. The kind is a closed set so that a declaration cannot invent a basis; the reference is where the obligation is named.

kind.description: legal_obligation: a statute requires the record (tax, accounting, employment). legal_claims: the record is needed to establish or defend a claim. contract: the record is needed to perform a contract that is still live. The concept names follow the legal-basis terms of the W3C Data Privacy Vocabulary where the two coincide, so a declaration maps onto a record of processing without translation.

reference.description: The obligation, named: the statute and section, the contract clause, the claim. A kind with no reference is a category and not a reason.

retain_for.description: How long the row is kept, measured from the column named in from. On expiry the row is deleted by the retention job (057 JB8 shape, named retention.purge); a basis with no expiry is a decision to hold personal data indefinitely, which DR5 does not admit.

from.description: The column the window counts from - issued_at, closed_at, terminated_at. Never created_at by default: the obligation usually runs from the event the row records, not from when the row was written.

stamp.description: DR5. Optional on anonymise and retain: two columns the erasure job writes when it reduces a row, so the row itself says it was reduced and for whom. This is 080 AE7's erased_at and erased_subjects pair, generalised: the audit store declares it and any store whose reduced rows must be distinguishable from rows that never carried the value may.

at.description: The instant column set to the erasure time.

subjects.description: The array column the erased subject's public id is appended to.

entry.description: One store, or one subject column of one store, and how it is treated on erasure and on export.

name.description: The table, collection, blob entity or external provider, named logically.

store.description: Which standard's rules the store is under: 025 for relational, 027 for document, 026 for blob. external is a backing service holding a copy the service placed there - a notification provider, an analytics vendor - reached through that provider's deletion interface by the erasure job, and never assumed to be covered by anyone else.

subject_column.description: The column, field or key that ties a row to the subject: the subject's public id, or a foreign key resolved through the entry named in via. For the subject's own root row it is that row's public id column. Required for every treatment but none.

via.description: The entry whose identity subject_column holds, where the subject is reached through another row. Entries with via are treated before the entry they name (DR4's dependency order), so a child never outlives its parent and a foreign key never dangles mid-run. A blob entry always carries via, because 026 makes a row the owner of every object.

tenant_scoped.description: Whether the store carries the isolation columns of 025 SD5. A scoped entry is treated for the tenant the request names; a global entry is treated when the subject holds no membership in any other tenant (DR4), or on every erasure where the inventory declares no membership entry.

membership.description: Marks the one entry whose rows are the subject's tenant memberships. It is what DR4 consults to decide whether global rows may go. At most one entry carries it; the corpus runner checks the count, which JSON Schema cannot.

treatment.description: DR5. delete: the rows are removed (025 SD12). anonymise: the rows are reduced to their structural columns plus retained_columns, every other value tombstoned, so the residue identifies nobody once every entry is treated. retain: the rows are reduced the same way but keep their subject linkage under legal_basis until retain_for expires. none: the store holds no personal data, and reason says why - present so a reader can tell considered from forgotten.

retained_columns.description: DR5. The ALLOWLIST of non-structural columns that survive reduction. Every column not named here and not structural is tombstoned - a free-text notes field included, because free text is where personal data hides. There is deliberately no denylist form: a list of columns to scrub is complete only until the next migration adds a column.

export.description: DR3. Whether the subject's rows in this entry are in the export package. False needs a reason a reviewer can hear: the rows are credential material (a session), or a derived projection of entries already exported (a search index), or a provider's copy of what the service already exports.

export_excludes.description: DR3. Columns withheld from the package although the entry is exported: a credential hash, or the columns that describe another person in a row shared between two subjects. Internal keys are excluded without being named, per 020 IP1.

reason.description: treatment none only: why this store holds nothing about a person.

allOf.description: DR1: an entry that holds personal data says which column names the person, whether it is tenant-scoped, and whether it is exported. An entry that holds none says why and nothing else.
DR5: a retained row has a legal basis with an expiry and an allowlist of what survives.
DR5: anonymisation is an allowlist, and it is declared even when empty - an empty list is a decision, an absent one is not.
DR5: a deleted row keeps nothing, so nothing is declared to survive and nothing is stamped.
026: a stored object is owned by a row, so a blob entry reaches its subject through that row and never directly.
An external provider's copy is reached through the provider, not through another entry.
DR3: excluding columns from an export that does not happen is a contradiction a reader would otherwise have to resolve.

service.description: The service whose stores these are, logically named as 055 AM1 names a source. One inventory per service, because 025 SD13 gives each service its own stores and no service can declare another's.

entries.description: Every store of the service. Completeness is checked against the engine's catalog by the coverage part of corpus.json: a table in the catalog with no entry is the finding.
